title: Running total
prompt: Show each session's id, minutes, and a running total of minutes in order of session_date then id, as running. Replace the ___.
hints: SUM with ORDER BY is cumulative.
solutions: SELECT id, minutes, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY session_date, id) AS running FROM sessions;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, minutes, SUM(minutes) OVER () AS running FROM sessions;
SELECT id, minutes, minutes AS running FROM sessions;

title: Per-user running total
prompt: Show each session's id and the running total of minutes for that user, by date then id, as running.
solutions: SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY session_date, id) AS running FROM sessions;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY session_date, id) AS running FROM sessions;
SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS running FROM sessions;

title: Three-reading average
prompt: Show each reading's id and the average temperature of it and the 2 previous readings in its city, rounded to 1 decimal, as moving_avg.
hints: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
solutions: SELECT id, ROUND(AVG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) AS moving_avg FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, ROUND(AVG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date), 1) AS moving_avg FROM readings;
SELECT id, ROUND(AVG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) AS moving_avg FROM readings;

title: Cumulative orders
prompt: Show each order's id, order_date, and the count of orders up to and including it, by date then id, as total_so_far.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id, order_date, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS total_so_far FROM orders;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, order_date, COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_so_far FROM orders;
SELECT id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY order_date DESC, id) AS total_so_far FROM orders;

title: Fewer rows than the frame
prompt: Show each reading's id and the sum of temperature for it and the 3 previous readings in its city, as sum_temp. Early rows use whatever exists.
hints: A frame just uses fewer rows when there aren't enough.
solutions: SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS sum_temp FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (ORDER BY reading_date ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS sum_temp FROM readings;
SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS sum_temp FROM readings;

title: Fix the tied dates
prompt: This running total gives the same value to sessions on one date, because ties share a default frame. Show id and running, adding id to the order. Fix it.
hints: A unique order makes the total step row by row.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 9, '2024-03-02', 9, 'web');

solutions: SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY session_date, id) AS running FROM sessions;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER () AS running FROM sessions;
SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY id DESC) AS running FROM sessions;

title: Date-based window
prompt: Dates can have gaps. Show each reading's id and the sum of temperature over the current and previous 2 calendar days for its city, as three_day_sum.
hints: RANGE on julianday works with date gaps.
solutions: SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY julianday(reading_date) RANGE BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS three_day_sum FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY julianday(reading_date) ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS three_day_sum FROM readings;
SELECT id, SUM(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY julianday(reading_date) RANGE BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS three_day_sum FROM readings;

title: Bus-style limit
prompt: Sessions run in id order. Show the id of the last session whose running total of minutes is at most 60.
hints: Calculate the running total, filter, and take the largest id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); UPDATE sessions SET minutes = 25 WHERE id IN (11, 12); UPDATE sessions SET minutes = 40 WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS running FROM sessions) WHERE running <= 60 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS running FROM sessions) WHERE running <= 60 ORDER BY id LIMIT 1;
SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE minutes <= 60 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;

title: Moving daily total
prompt: Dates can repeat or have gaps. First total minutes per date, then show each session_date and its 3-calendar-day moving average, as moving_avg. That's the total for the date and the 2 days before it, divided by 3 and rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by date.
hints: Total per day in a CTE, then use RANGE and divide by 3.0.
solutions: WITH d AS (SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date) SELECT session_date, ROUND(SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY julianday(session_date) RANGE BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) / 3.0, 2) AS moving_avg FROM d ORDER BY session_date;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date) SELECT session_date, ROUND(AVG(total) OVER (ORDER BY julianday(session_date) ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg FROM d ORDER BY session_date;
SELECT session_date, ROUND(AVG(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY session_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg FROM sessions ORDER BY session_date;

title: Running revenue
prompt: Show each order's id, its revenue (price times quantity) as revenue, and the running total by order id as running.
hints: Total per order first, then a window over it.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: WITH r AS (SELECT i.order_id AS id, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id) SELECT id, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS running FROM r;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.order_id AS id, p.price * i.quantity AS revenue, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) OVER (ORDER BY i.order_id) AS running FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;
WITH r AS (SELECT i.order_id AS id, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id) SELECT id, revenue, revenue AS running FROM r;
